elements.text: Temperature ≥ 38°C now or in past 3 days 38
Manage urgently:

If dehydration likely, give oral rehydration solution (ORS) and observe. If unable to drink, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens. If IV rehydration needed or no better with oral rehydration after 2 hours, refer.
If worsening weakness of leg/s, refer urgently.
WEAKNESS OR TIREDNESS

Approach to patient with weakness or tiredness not needing urgent attention • Look for a cause for tiredness if it persists and patient is unable to complete routine tasks and it disrupts work, social and family life. • First check symptoms, medications, mental health and long-term health conditions:

Check symptoms • If cough, weight loss, night sweats or fever, check for TB 102. • If patient has difficulty sleeping 99. • If weight gain, low mood, dry skin, constipation or cold intolerance, check TSH. If abnormal, refer to doctor. • Check for symptoms/signs suggestive of cancer or if eligible for cancer screening 194.

Check medications • If on abacavir or zidovudine, check for urgent side effects 131. • Chlorphenamine, enalapril, amlodipine, fluoxetine, amitriptyline, metoclopramide, sodium valproate, phenytoin and spironolactone can cause weakness or tiredness. Discuss with doctor.

Check mental health • In the past month, has patient felt down/ depressed/hopeless or little interest/pleasure in doing things? If yes to either 159. • In the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks1/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription/over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165. • If none of the above, assess for stress and anxiety 98.

Check long-term health conditions • Test for HIV 124. If HIV positive, give routine care 126. • Check for pregnancy 174. • Check Hb. If < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely 44. • Check for diabetes 19. • If patient has a life-limiting illness, also give palliative care 191.
